# Chapter 8 — Series Progression

::: {.callout-note}
## In this chapter
A milestone summary of what the OrgPath governance substrate now covers after Part Twelve, when in-guest machine state governance closes the gap identified in Chapter One. This chapter restates the full scope of governance domains that OrgTree and OrgPath now drive end to end, and previews the one remaining document — the Part Thirteen capstone reporting layer that makes every enforcement action and compliance signal legible by organizational position.
:::

With Part Twelve complete, the OrgPath governance substrate has reached the operating system layer. The governance perimeter is no longer bounded by what the Azure control plane can observe from the outside of a machine. It extends inside the guest operating system through Guest Configuration packages that enforce tier-appropriate DSC baselines on every Arc-enrolled server, report their compliance state through the same Azure Policy and Resource Graph infrastructure used throughout the series, alert through the same Sentinel workspace that processes identity and network governance signals, and respond automatically to OrgTree tier changes through the same pipeline event model that governs identity lifecycle, RBAC assignments, and certificate issuance. The machine state governance gap described in Chapter One is closed.

The full scope of what the architecture now covers is worth stating plainly at this point in the series. OrgTree provides the versioned organizational hierarchy registry — the authoritative record of every organizational node, its parent relationships, its tier classification, and its change history. OrgPath provides the structured positional attribute that every governed resource carries as a tag, derived from OrgTree and maintained by the propagation pipeline. Identity lifecycle through Lifecycle Workflows is governed by OrgPath segment. Privileged access through PIM is governed by OrgPath tier. Security event correlation in Sentinel is enriched by OrgPath context. Azure RBAC assignments are scoped and maintained by OrgPath segment. Device compliance through Intune and Defender is governed by OrgPath tier. DNS zone authority is delegated by OrgPath segment. Cloud PKI certificate issuance is constrained by OrgPath segment. Information protection labels in Microsoft Purview are assigned based on OrgPath segment. B2B guest access is governed by the OrgPath of the inviting principal's organizational node. Service principal lifecycle is governed by the OrgPath of the owning team. And now, the in-guest configuration state of every Arc-enrolled server is governed by the OrgPath tier of the organizational node the server belongs to.

One document remains in this series. Part Thirteen constructs the capstone reporting layer: a unified governance posture reporting model fed by governance repository JSON exports, Sentinel KQL query results, Intune compliance data, Defender compliance signals, and Resource Graph Guest Configuration compliance states. Every governance signal produced by the pipelines established in Parts One through Twelve is sliced by OrgPath and presented in a stakeholder-accessible reporting layer organized by organizational position. The capstone report answers the question that every governance architecture ultimately exists to answer: for any given part of the organization, what is its current posture against the standards the architecture requires, what has drifted, what is being remediated, and what requires human attention. Part Thirteen closes the substrate loop by making every enforcement action and every compliance signal legible to the organizational stakeholders who own the governance posture and are accountable for its maintenance.
